title: Heap Journey
description: Heap design, top-k selection, k-way merging, two heaps, scheduling, and graph frontiers.

journey.outcome: Choose the right heap ordering and size, then compose heaps with streams and queues.

connections.check-array-is-max-heap: Start by recognizing heap order in an array-backed complete tree. A heap guarantees a parent-child relationship, not that the whole array is sorted.
connections.min-heap-implementation: Turn the parent-child invariant into operations. Flip the comparison for a min-heap and repair only the path disturbed by an insertion or removal.
connections.heap-sort: Reuse heap repair to sort in place. A max-heap moves the largest remaining item to the sorted suffix; the active heap boundary shrinks after each extraction.
connections.last-stone-weight: Use the heap as a changing collection rather than a sorting tool. Removing the two largest values can create a new candidate that must rejoin the remaining priorities.
connections.kth-smallest-element-in-an-array: Avoid sorting everything when only one rank matters. Retain k candidates in a max-heap so the least desirable retained candidate is always removable.
connections.kth-largest-element-in-an-array: Mirror the previous selection problem. Keep the k largest candidates in a min-heap; its root is the smallest retained value and therefore the kth largest overall.
connections.sort-a-nearly-sorted-array: Use a different reason to bound heap size: every value is at most k positions from its sorted place, so only the next k + 1 candidates can be the next output.
connections.k-closest-points-to-origin: Return to bounded selection and replace the numeric key with squared distance. A max-heap removes the farthest retained point when a closer candidate arrives.
connections.top-k-frequent-elements: Change the priority again, from distance to frequency. Count first, then retain the k strongest candidates with a min-heap and an explicit tie-break.
connections.top-k-frequent-words: Keep frequency selection, but make tie-breaking part of the contract. When retaining only k words, the worst retained word has lower frequency or lexicographically larger spelling.
connections.kth-largest-element-in-a-stream: Make your kth-largest heap persistent. Each new arrival only updates the same k candidates; recomputing or sorting the whole history is unnecessary.
connections.merge-k-sorted-arrays: Move from one incoming stream to k sorted streams. Keep only the current head of each stream in a min-heap and replace the head you consume.
connections.merge-k-sorted-lists: Reuse the k-way merge exactly, changing only the cursor representation. A node's next pointer replaces the array-and-offset pair.
connections.kth-smallest-element-in-a-sorted-matrix: Treat each sorted row as a stream, but stop after k extractions instead of materializing the whole merge. Sorted columns also enable an alternative value-space binary search.
connections.find-k-pairs-with-smallest-sums: Build the streams implicitly: fixing one value in the first sorted array creates a sorted row of pair sums with the second. Advance only the row whose head was consumed.
connections.minimum-cost-to-connect-ropes: Unlike merging sorted streams, extraction now creates a new candidate. Reinsert each combined rope and justify why combining the two smallest remaining lengths minimizes repeated cost.
connections.find-median-from-data-stream: One heap exposes an extreme; a median needs a boundary between two halves. Maintain a max-heap below that boundary and a min-heap above it, balanced after each insertion.
connections.sliding-window-median: Interview stretch: add expiry to the two-heap median. A departing value may be buried, so distinguish live sizes from physical heap sizes and remove stale entries before using a root.
connections.reorganize-string: Return to frequency priorities and make the previously chosen character temporarily unavailable. Holding one candidate aside prevents adjacent equal characters without giving up greedy selection.
connections.task-scheduler: Coordinate two structures with different jobs: a max-heap ranks ready tasks and a FIFO queue records cooldown release times. Priority alone cannot tell you when a task is legal.
connections.minimum-number-of-platforms-required-for: Change the priority from task frequency to resource release time. A min-heap of departures identifies reusable platforms; peak simultaneous occupancy determines the required capacity.
connections.dijkstras-algorithm: Generalize choosing the next event to choosing the cheapest graph frontier. With nonnegative edges, the smallest valid tentative distance can be finalized; obsolete heap entries must be skipped.
